title: Embedding quantization safeguard: calibration harness and cosine-drift validation
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary:
We need a repeatable, production-ready calibration and validation workflow for embedding models when converting to INT8 and FP16 inference profiles. The goal is to produce quantization profiles that meet unit-cost objectives while keeping cosine similarity drift under strict thresholds for downstream retrieval and semantic search workloads. This ticket delivers: a calibration harness that produces stable scale/zero parameters, a drift validation suite that computes distributional and pairwise cosine regressions, and a gating policy for rollout (canary thresholds + automatic rollback hooks).

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Produce quantization profiles for the primary embedding family (enc-3a, enc-3b) for INT8 and FP16 that: average cosine shift < 0.005 over representative eval set, 95th percentile shift < 0.02, and no more than 3% of vectors drop below retrieval-recall threshold for top-10.
- Automation: nightly calibration runs against anchor datasets; generate PR with profile artifacts and a validation report; flag failures to #embed-ops Slack and create ENG ticket if regressions exceed thresholds.
- Rollout gating: Canary at 1% traffic with drift/recall monitoring for first 24 hours; auto-airgap/rollback if any monitored metric crosses critical threshold.

Calibration workflow (high level):
1) Data selection: sample balanced calibration corpus with 100k vectors across domains (queries, docs, code, short/long). See datasets field.
2) Preprocess: normalize tokens, apply same preprocessing pipeline used in production (tokenizer parity).
3) Layerwise activation capture: run fp32 baseline forward pass to capture activation ranges for key MLP and attention projection matrices.
4) Scale computation: compute per-channel symmetric/asymmetric scales for INT8 and FP16 mixed-path where appropriate. Persist both deterministic and stochastic calibration outputs.
5) Profile export: emit JSON profile with metadata (model hash, dataset hash, commit, exact calibration flags).
6) Validation: run embedding similarity checks and downstream recall simulations against eval suite.

Datasets and eval sets (quick listing):
- anchor-calib-100k: mixed domains (news, qa, product, code) — used for scale computation
- stable-eval-10k: high-signal pairs with human-annotated similarity — primary cosine drift metric
- retrieval-sim-50k: synthetic retrieval workload to compute top-k recall change
- drift-smoke-1k: small fast-run set for CI pre-merge checks
Links to sources: GCS:gs://redwood-eval/anchor-calib-100k, Notebook: drive:/Shared/embed-calib/playbook.ipynb

Metrics we compute:
- mean_cosine_shift: mean(|cos_fp32 - cos_quant|) across stable-eval pairs
- p95_cosine_shift: 95th percentile of absolute cosine shift
- recall_delta_top10: (recall_quant - recall_fp32) for retrieval-sim workloads
- vector_dropout_rate: percent of vectors with L2 norm degraded below threshold causing retrieval miss
- calibration_stability: variance of scale params across 3 independent seeds
- CI_time: time to run full validation (target < 90m for 100k sample)

Experiment notes (initial runs):
- Ran INT8 symmetric/channel-wise with per-layer clipping on enc-3a vs enc-3b. Observed mean_cosine_shift ~0.0048 (good), p95 ~0.018, recall_delta_top10 ~-1.9%. FP16 path shows near-zero drift but higher memory cost; INT8 offers 2.8x token-cost improvement in microbenchmarks.
- Failure modes: outlier tokens in short-code domain produce large local shifts; mitigation was to extend per-channel calibration windows and enable 8-bit residual scaling for projection layers.

Implementation tasks and PRs: (placeholders / in-flight)
- infra: add nightly calibration job + artifact storage (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/840)
- runtime: load-profile API + deterministic seed path (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2213)
- validation: drift suite and dashboard panels (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1198)
- notebooks: drive:/Shared/embed-calib/experiments/2026-03-04-notebook.ipynb

Rollout plan and gating rules:
- Stage 0 (local/dev): smoke CI on drift-smoke-1k, blocked if mean_cosine_shift > 0.01
- Stage 1 (canary): 1% traffic for 24 hrs; collect metrics at 5m granularity. Block/rollback if recall_delta_top10 < -3% or p95_cosine_shift > 0.03 or vector_dropout_rate > 5%
- Stage 2 (ramp): 10% for 48 hrs with continued monitoring; manual approval to 100%
- Emergency rollback: deterministic fallback to fp32 path with immediate routing switch if critical thresholds observed.

Risks & mitigation:
- Dataset drift: keep a rotating anchor dataset and weekly re-calibration. Add telemetry to detect domain drift and trigger re-calibration automatically.
- Non-deterministic calibration: run 3 seeds and only accept profiles with stability <= threshold; if unstable, mark profile experimental and require manual sign-off.
- Cost vs quality tradeoff: maintain a Pareto dashboard showing cost savings vs recall loss to help product decisions.

Acceptance tests (automatable):
- CI job that runs drift-smoke-1k and fails if mean_cosine_shift >= 0.01
- Nightly run that posts a report artifact to GCS and creates an ENG ticket if any metric breaches soft thresholds

Done criteria:
- Automation pipeline merged and scheduled
- Two embedding families (enc-3a/enc-3b) have signed INT8/FP16 profiles with artifacts stored and PRs + validation reports
- Console panels for mean_cosine_shift and recall_delta_top10 inverted into alerts
- Runbook added to drive:/Runbooks/embed-quant-safeguard.md
acceptance_criteria: 1) INT8 and FP16 profiles exported to artifact bucket with metadata; 2) mean_cosine_shift < 0.005 and p95 < 0.02 on stable-eval-10k for both families; 3) nightlies run without stability failures for 3 consecutive days; 4) console alerts present and thresholded; 5) canary gating implemented and tested
experiments: - INT8 symmetric per-channel vs asymmetric profiling; - FP16 conversion with fallback mixing for projection layers; - Per-layer clip vs global clip strategies; - Residual-scaling variant for short-sequence code domain
results_summary: Initial calibration runs met mean_cosine_shift targets for enc-3a; enc-3b showed a p95 spike driven by code-domain outliers. Fixes applied (residual scaling and extended calibration windows) reduced p95 by ~30%. INT8 gives ~2.8x cost improvement vs fp32; FP16 preserves quality with 1.2x memory cost increase.
